description: For NASA Space Apps, we are developing Terra2Mars AI — an AI-powered platform that helps discover Earth locations that are most similar to possible Mars and Moon settlement environments.Our team brings skills in Python, AI/ML, FastAPI, React/Next.js, backend development, APIs, databases, data visualization, and intelligent systems.
summary:
TerraNova (Terra2Mars AI) is a planetary analogue discovery platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Before space agencies deploy astronauts to the Moon or rovers to Mars, mission equipment must be tested in extreme Earth environments.

Because Earth cannot physically recreate a vacuum or −230°C cold traps, TerraNova matches measurable operational challenges. Using open NASA satellite data, it screens all 78,247 land cells on Earth across 8 environmental and terrain criteria—including dryness, sterile vegetation, temperature swings, and ruggedness.

Scoring uses 100% deterministic math with a weighted geometric mean, where active failures strictly veto unsuitable locations. Results are visualized on an interactive 3D globe with high-resolution terrain analysis, providing a transparent, scientifically validated screening engine for future space missions.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

TerraNova scans Earth’s entire land surface (78,247 grid cells at ~55 km resolution) to find locations that best match the terrain and climate of permanent Moon base sites (e.g., Shackleton Rim) and Mars exploration targets (e.g., Jezero Crater). It scores each cell across 8 environmental criteria—dryness, zero vegetation, temperature ranges, thermal swings, slope, and roughness—using deterministic mathematical formulas, then displays ranked sites on an interactive 3D globe.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Data-Driven Discovery: Replaces anecdotal site selection with an objective, global scan.
  • 100% Explainable: No black-box AI guessing; every score is pure math with a transparent breakdown.
  • Novelty Detection: Automatically flags whether a winning site is near an established test ground or a brand-new candidate.
  • Offline & Lightweight: Completely self-contained, requiring zero internet connectivity at runtime.

3. What is the intended impact?

It reduces the cost and risk of lunar and Martian missions. Space agencies, commercial companies, and researchers can rapidly identify the best, most realistic terrestrial proving grounds to test rovers, EVA suits, drills, and life-support habitats before launching to space.

4. What tools, languages, software, and data were used?

  • Languages: Python 3.12, JavaScript (HTML5 Canvas, ES modules).
  • Backend & Compute: FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, Zarr.
  • Frontend & 3D: Three.js, OrbitControls (zero external CSS/JS frameworks).
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER (climate reanalysis), NASA GIBS (MODIS NDVI & Blue Marble), Zenodo (MODIS Land Surface Temperature), AWS Open Data (Terrarium DEMs), Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery, and Natural Earth vectors.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Matching Challenges, Not Physics: Recognizes that Earth cannot copy a vacuum or −230°C, so it creatively matches the closest attainable engineering proxies.
  • Strict Veto Math: Uses a weighted geometric mean where a total failure in one active requirement (e.g., dense rainforest vegetation) strictly disqualifies a site from winning.
  • "God’s Eye" 3D Explorer: A local 3D terrain mode with dynamic sun simulations—including a 1.5° lunar polar sun angle—and an automated 15° rover mobility slope hazard evaluation.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scale Mismatch: Translated fine rover-scale measurements (5–50 m) into calibrated Earth percentile classes to match global 55 km grid cells.
  • Earth Clamping: Clamped extraterrestrial extremes to Earth's 99.5th percentile to prevent breaking mathematical scales.
  • Scientific Provenance: Ensured every single number, criterion, and target profile is linked to an official NASA, ESA, or peer-reviewed publication.
  • Geographic Diversity: Implemented spatial distance spreading and per-country result caps so single large deserts wouldn't monopolize the top rankings.
